title: Oases of Life: May 2016
place: Mariana back-arc spreading center hydrothermal vent field, western Pacific (EX1605 Leg 1)
audio: track present in source (the compilation has narration/music); mute it
notes: 0-8.2 s: a thick, jet-BLACK smoke column pours straight up out of a chimney while pale vent shrimp and white crabs crawl all over the rock around it (very eerie, the best part). The camera is static, with a slight push-in. The smoke column is at x~0.40-0.50 and fills the frame top to bottom. 8.3-12 s: a close-up of a rusty-brown chimney (soft focus), then 12-14 s a blurry white seafloor patch. Best seconds 0-8 (two 3.4 s cuts fit: 0-3.4 and 4.2-7.6). The source is 1280x720, upscaled to 1920x1080. The source compilation also has scientist interviews (faces at 28-35 s and elsewhere); the cut starts 36.1 s, after the interview ends at ~35.9 s, so no people. No logos or text in this window. Animals (shrimp/crabs) are only background.
fact_en: During the 2016 Deepwater Exploration of the Marianas, NOAA discovered a new active high-temperature 'black smoker' hydrothermal vent field on the Mariana back-arc spreading center, composed of multiple chimneys, including one that was over 30 meters (98 feet) tall.
